definitions.explanation: Someone who refuses to change their mind or yield, even when they know they are wrong. Also used as a な-adjective to describe such behavior.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}は{意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りだ。
{意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りな{性格|せいかく}で{損|そん}をすることがある。
examples.english: Being stubborn sometimes works against you.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りだから、{自分|じぶん}から{謝|あやま}ることは{絶対|ぜったい}にしない。
examples.english: He's so stubborn that he would never apologize first.

notes:
USAGE:
Can function as both a noun and a な-adjective ({意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りな{人|ひと}). Generally carries a negative nuance, suggesting someone is being unreasonably obstinate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りな{性格|せいかく} (stubborn personality)
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りな{人|ひと} (stubborn person)
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}りで{損|そん}をする (lose out by being stubborn)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn — more neutral, can imply steadfastness; often used for older people
- {強情|ごうじょう}: obstinate — emphasizes refusal to yield, slightly more formal
